answer: Resist Sybils with cluster-wide throttling: identities are grouped by observable links — shared devices, payment rails, or identical behavior — and each cluster gets one collective rate limit tied to an anchor member verified first. Like trees in an orchard sharing one water supply, extra identities do not add capacity; they split the same quota. A ripple of abuse from one member throttles the whole cluster, so a farm of thousands gains no more throughput than a single honest agent, while honest clusters keep full speed.
